contexts.text: Hence their lavers were of brass... because brass represented the good of external worship, which is the same as natural good.

The lavers, which were of brass, were placed outside the temple; namely, the brazen sea, and the ten brazen lavers, and the laver of brass from which Aaron and his sons washed themselves... by which was signified that external or natural things alone were being purified; and unless these are purified internal things... can never inflow.
Hence it is that baptism... is called the Laver of Regeneration.
